arrival_or_introduction_evidence: Introduced Apis mellifera status direct; exact arrival timing and before-after transition unavailable
community_or_interaction_change: Direct visitor rates plus diurnal nectar standing crop/production; endemic white-eyes stop feeding when honeybee activity lowers nectar standing crop
effectiveness_evidence: Direct bagging/caging comparison of pollination efficiency; honeybees less efficient than endemic white-eyes on two endemic Sideroxylon species
reproductive_response_evidence: Experimental pollination-performance consequence direct, but not a neutral honeybee-free before-after reproductive transition
strongest_supported_inference: Introduced honeybees can alter realized nectar access and are less efficient pollinators than endemic birds in the focal Sideroxylon system
unresolved_boundary: No neutral honeybee-free control site; introduction history, source plant state and full matched transition remain unresolved

arrival_or_introduction_evidence: Introduced honeybee dominance and spread across main/satellite islands direct; exact arrival transition not matched to focal plant response
community_or_interaction_change: Twelve-island visitor survey shows native solitary bees dominate preserved satellite networks whereas Apis dominates main islands and spreads nearby
effectiveness_evidence: For Psychotria homalosperma, honeybee morphology/behavior causes unidirectional pollen transfer between floral morphs
reproductive_response_evidence: Hand/open pollination, pollen-tube observations and fruit set direct; long-styled flowers set fruit 1.7–38 times more than short-styled flowers
strongest_supported_inference: Across complementary Ogasawara studies, introduced honeybee dominance is linked to network restructuring and a focal plant mechanism that creates asymmetric pollen transfer and reproduction
unresolved_boundary: Network and focal-plant studies are not one prespecified matched transition; original pollinator identity is inferred rather than observed historically

arrival_or_introduction_evidence: Braunsapis puangensis first recorded in 2007 and later mapped widely; Amegilla pulchra also introduced into a fauna lacking native buzz pollinators
community_or_interaction_change: Direct distribution, foraging and plant-visitor data; 2019 study records 165 bee-plant interactions across 27 plant species and shows exotic bees collectively dominate visits to many plants
effectiveness_evidence: Visitor identity and functional novelty direct; plant-specific pollination efficiency not measured across the network
reproductive_response_evidence: No linked native-plant reproductive response; weed-pollination consequences remain interaction-based rather than seed-output causal tests
strongest_supported_inference: A recent pollinator-arrival chronology can be connected to contemporary network occupation and functional novelty within the same island system
unresolved_boundary: The chain stops before plant reproductive response/effectiveness, so it cannot satisfy the full Chapter 2 contract
